gap: No result ChatGPT got states the cost per square foot of picture for floor-rising screens. From maker-store prices on 2026-11-11, the Elite Kestrel Tab-Tension 3 122" in matte-white CineWhite works out to about $43.5/sq ft, while the UST light-rejecting screens cost about $63.5–66/sq ft: the VIVIDSTORM S PRO Plus 130" at about $63.5 and the Elite Kestrel Tab-Tension 2 CLR 3 121" at about $65.9.
standout_why: I compared against projector-screen-guide.com, projectorverdict.com (motorized) and primeareviews.com. projector-screen-guide.com gives image sizes and one housing-minus-image width (VIVIDSTORM 100": 98.4 − 87.17 in), but it shows 'Check price' instead of prices, so it has no cost per area. projectorverdict.com gives VIVIDSTORM S PRO prices by size and the Kestrel at $1,923 but no image area. primeareviews.com gives only price bands. None of them divides price by picture area, and none separates matte-white screens from UST light-rejecting screens on cost.
decides: This shows the price gap the shopper pays for UST light-rejecting material. At similar sizes (121–130") it costs about $20–22 more per sq ft, roughly 45–50% more than Elite's matte-white Kestrel Tab-Tension 3. So if the room can be kept dark, or the projector is not a UST, the Kestrel Tab-Tension 3 122" ($1,923) gives the most picture per dollar. With a UST projector in a lit room, the VIVIDSTORM S PRO Plus 130" ($3,187) costs slightly less per sq ft than Elite's CLR 3 121" ($2,864), even though its total price is higher. Treat this as a partial result. Store rate limits stopped me getting per-size prices for the S PRO, AWOL and Kestrel CineGrey 4D, so the three figures here are the only ones fully sourced.
